summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 5 upside misses — COHR +14%, ABNB +12%, VST +11%, APP +10%, NRG +10%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AXON -18%, MCHP -10%, CHTR -6%, PODD -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: AXON (-18.18%) — Q3 earnings miss (EPS ~$1.72 vs ~$1.90 est, revenue ~2.4% light) with a guidance cut, plus a $1.2B Skydio deal and margin pressure from memory costs; analysts cut targets. Sources conflict on the exact drop date. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: AXON is a mid/large-cap growth name no strategy covers. It was also an earnings-gap move, and the decline began on the post-results session, so a bot working from post-market signals could not have positioned ahead of it.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day catalyst found. Searches returned only older COHR moves (AI optics demand, earnings, analyst target raises), and the price levels in them don't match today's 192.81 close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: COHR is a mid/large-cap optical/photonics name tied to the AI-datacenter theme, and no strategy covers it. With no news-reactive trigger either, a sector/AI-optics momentum move was missed.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a liquid AI-hardware/optical-networking sub-universe (COHR, LITE, CIEN, ANET) to the momentum strategy, admitting names with a ≥+8% day on ≥1.5x 20-day average volume and a ≥$1B market cap floor.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 earnings beat (reported Nov 5 after close): revenue +19% to ~$4.87B, EPS $3.16 vs $2.85 est, bookings +16%, FY growth outlook raised, plus a new $12B buyback. Part of the EPS beat was a tax item.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (large-cap consumer-internet/travel name). The move was an overnight earnings gap (~$170 to ~$189), so a post-open momentum or news filter would see it as already priced in and too extended to chase.
top_movers.suggestion: Add ABNB and similar large-cap travel/consumer-internet names to the news-reactive universe, with an earnings-gap rule that enters on gap ≥ +8% when first-hour volume is ≥ 2× average and price holds above the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Unconfirmed: sources are undated and conflict on price. They point to a Google Cloud EPYC/TPU deal, an Oppenheimer upgrade after earnings, and rotation out of Nvidia into AMD and other chip stocks.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AMD is a large-cap semiconductor name. Only the news-reactive strategies trade it, and they likely passed because sentiment-gate and buzz-fade skip or fade headline-driven gaps like this one.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semis (AMD, MU, AMAT) to the momentum universe, and let news-reactive-sentiment-gate pass a name on a confirmed upgrade or partnership headline when the gap is at least +5% on volume of 1.5x average or more.

top_movers.catalyst: Rebound after Q3 results, 2027 EBITDA guidance ($7.7-8.5B) and a $1.5B buyback add-on, following a ~14% data-center power selloff on Nov 4. Coverage is dated Nov 6; I found no separate Nov 9 news.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: VST is a ~$40B+ mid/large-cap independent power producer (AI/data-center power theme) that no strategy covers. The move was also earnings- and rebound-driven, so a post-results gap would likely have failed gap/RSI filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap IPP/AI-power names (VST, CEG, NRG, TLN) to the momentum-trader universe, and let its gap-up filter release post-earnings gaps of at least +7% when volume is at least 1.5x average within the first 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst: searches returned nothing dated 2026-11-09. Likely a continued post-Q3-earnings / ad-tech rebound or sector move; unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: APP is a large-cap, high-beta ad-tech/software name that no strategy includes. If it was earnings-related, the gap was also likely priced in before a post-signal entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta large-cap tech (e.g. APP) to the momentum-trader universe, or add a dynamic-universe rule admitting any name with a ≥+8% day on ≥2× average volume, so next analogue is screened.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 2026 beat (adj. EPS $4.68 vs ~$3.4 est, EBITDA +67% on LS Power assets), reaffirmed 2026 guidance, set 2027 guidance, and announced a $4B asset sale funding $3B of buybacks.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: NRG is a mid/large-cap independent power producer (utilities/IPP). The move was an earnings-gap catalyst, so a post-results momentum filter would also have been late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add US mid-cap utilities/IPPs (e.g. NRG, VST, CEG) to the momentum universe, and let the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap of +5% or more on volume of at least 1.5x average.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 earnings miss (EPS ~$1.72 vs ~$1.90 est, revenue ~2.4% light) with a guidance cut, plus a $1.2B Skydio deal and margin pressure from memory costs; analysts cut targets. Sources conflict on the exact drop date.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AXON is a mid/large-cap growth name no strategy covers. It was also an earnings-gap move, and the decline began on the post-results session, so a bot working from post-market signals could not have positioned ahead of it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AXON-type US mid-cap growth names to the universe, and add an earnings-gate rule that flags post-earnings gaps of -8% or worse for avoidance or a short-watch. If the bot can't short, a no-op is fine.

top_movers.catalyst: Weak Dec-qtr guidance (EPS $0.87-0.95 vs $0.94 est.), foundry/assembly supply constraints and CEO 'data center bubble' remarks. Sources date the -10% close to Nov 6; MCHP rose ~5% on Nov 9.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap analog/MCU semi). Even in universe, this was an earnings-gap move that happened a session earlier, so any Nov 9 signal would see a bounce, not a fresh drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Check the data feed's date alignment for movers, since the -10.02% at 58.35 matches Nov 6 and not Nov 9. Separately, add large-cap semis to the news-reactive universe with an earnings-gap rule (gap ≤ -8% on guidance miss → skip or flag for mean reversion).

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day catalyst found; the drop looks like continued post-Q1 selling on broadband subscriber losses and churn worries, possibly with Liberty Broadband-related share-sale headlines.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHTR is a large-cap cable/telecom name that no strategy includes. A grinding, news-light decline after a big earnings crash would also fail gap-up and momentum entry filters.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change: the bot is long-only and can't short this decline. If it needs coverage, add large-cap telecom/cable to the mean-reversion universe with a min-ADV filter and an earnings-crash cooldown of about 60 days.)

top_movers.catalyst: No Nov 9 news found. Likely continued post-Q3 (Nov 4) drift: record margins but a conservative 2027 outlook, flat US patient starts and one-off reserve boosts to international growth.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap medtech, ~$10B). The drop had no fresh same-day catalyst, so a news-reactive bot had no trigger, and the earnings gap came days earlier.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap healthcare names with 20-day ADV above $100M to the mean-reversion universe, so a -6% non-event day on a name that recently reported can be evaluated against its RSI(14) oversold threshold.
